# 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 378r

---

**1** David consulted with all his military commanders — officers over thousands and over hundreds — and with every other leader. **2** Then he addressed the entire assembly of Israel: "If you are willing, and if it is the LORD our God's will, let us send messages to our fellow Israelites who remain throughout the land, including the priests and Levites in their towns and pasturelands, inviting them to join us. **3** Let us bring back the ark of our God, because we neglected it during Saul's reign."

**4** The whole assembly enthusiastically agreed, because everyone saw that it was the right thing to do. **5** So David gathered all Israel together — from the Shihor River on the Egyptian border all the way to Lebo-hamath in the north — to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim. **6** David and all Israel went to Baalah (that is, Kiriath-jearim) in Judah to bring back the ark of God the LORD, who is enthroned between the cherubim — the ark over which his Name is proclaimed.

**7** They transported the ark of God on a brand-new cart from the house of Abinadab, with Uzzah and Ahio guiding the cart. **8** David and all Israel celebrated wildly before God, singing with all their might and playing lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.

**9** But when they arrived at the threshing floor of Chidon, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the ark. **10** The LORD's anger blazed against Uzzah, and God struck him dead on the spot — because he had touched the ark. He died right there in God's presence.

**11** David was shaken — first angry that the LORD had burst out against Uzzah (that place has been called Perez-uzzah — "the Outbreak against Uzzah" — ever since), **12** and then afraid of God. "How can I ever bring the ark of God to be with me?" he said.

**13** So David did not move the ark to the City of David. Instead, he diverted it to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. **14** The ark of God stayed with Obed-edom's family in his house for three months. And the LORD blessed Obed-edom's household and everything he owned.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 3 — "We neglected it during Saul's reign":** David's first public act as king is to correct Saul's greatest failure. In 10:14, Saul died because "he did not seek the LORD." David's opening move is precisely to seek (*darash*) the symbol of God's presence. The Chronicler constructs a perfect contrast.

**Verse 7 — A brand-new cart:** This detail matters enormously for the story's theology. The Philistines sent the ark back on a new cart (1 Samuel 6) — and it worked. Israel imitates the Philistine method instead of following the Torah's prescription (Levites carrying it on poles). The failure is a failure of scriptural obedience, not of good intentions.

**Verse 10-12 — From anger to fear:** David's emotional journey in two verses moves from rage to terror. The anger is human — "Why did this happen when we were doing something good?" The fear is theological — "If God's holiness is this dangerous, how do I approach it at all?" This tension drives the narrative forward to chapter 15, where David finds the answer: follow the proper order.

**Verse 14 — Obed-edom's blessing:** A quietly brilliant detail. The ark that killed a man now blesses a household. The ark is not inherently destructive — it responds to how it is approached. This three-month interlude gives David time to learn the right way.

*— PNEUMA*
